implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.is_valid_move() checks emptiness and uses _flips_in_direction across all DIRECTIONS; Board.get_valid_moves() returns all legal squares.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Flip opponent discs when a disc is placed
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.place_disc() gathers flips from all directions via _flips_in_direction and updates the grid accordingly.
Board.count_discs() returns (black, white); Game.refresh() and Game.end_game() call Gui.update_score() which shows the live score.

implemented_requirements.requirement: End the game when the board is full or no valid moves remain for either player
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game.advance_turn() checks board.is_full() and that both players have no moves, then calls end_game().
Game.current_player tracks whose turn it is; advance_turn() switches players, applies pass when next player has no moves, and informs the GUI.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Graphical board rendering with move hints
implemented_requirements.evidence: Gui.draw_board() draws the 8×8 grid, discs, and highlights cells in the valid_moves list.
Gui.on_click() translates canvas clicks to board coordinates and forwards them to Game.handle_click(); Gui.on_restart() calls Game.reset().

implemented_requirements.requirement: Entry point to start the application
implemented_requirements.evidence: main.py creates Gui and Game instances and calls game.start() which runs the Tkinter mainloop.

critical_issues: The code depends on a graphical environment (Tkinter). Running in a headless CI environment would fail, but this is expected for a GUI application.
Board.place_disc() does not internally verify that the target cell is empty; it relies on Game.handle_click() to have performed the validation first.
judge.summary: All core Reversi features—legal‑move detection, disc flipping, turn handling with pass, automatic game termination, and live score display—are fully implemented and wired through a functional Tkinter GUI. The code is self‑contained and appears ready to run, with only minor assumptions about the presence of a display. No missing functionality or stub code was found, so the submission meets the benchmark requirements.
